names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 12 iunie, «Sfântul Cuvios Petru Athonitul».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 12 Ιουνίου, «Όσιος Πέτρος ο Θεοφόρος ο εν Άθω ασκήσας», with the rank word and the epithets left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 12. јун ст. ст., „Преподобни Петар Атонски“ — Преподобни is the rank and comes off, and the by-name Атонски stays. **THE FOLD IS DELIBERATELY AVOIDED**: `foldchk.py` returns `peter-of-bulgaria` and `peter-of-lampsacus`, both `sr`, for a bare «Петар», and nothing at all for «Петар Атонски». The heading gives the by-name, so §6’s rule to keep it decides the form and no third folder joins that string.

Read out of the name link behind the calendar's line for 12 июня ст. ст., name page 1767, «Петр Афонский, прп.». The line declines both words («Петра Афонского»); the rank «прп.» is not stored with the form.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 12 июня ст. ст. — «Прп. Петра Афонского (734)»

attestations.note: The day's second entry, and the same menologion number the folder's romanian, greek and serbian rows already carry, so there is no second day here. THE LINE GIVES 734 AND `dates` WAS NOT WRITTEN FROM IT: it is the first year any calendar has given this folder, the only witness to it is this day line, and the Russian life page behind it was not opened — so it is recorded here and in the life and nowhere else. The `ru` form is read out of the name link behind «Петра», name page 1767, «Петр Афонский, прп.». Three hymns are taken: «Тропарь преподобных Онуфрия и Петра» глас 4, which is the common of venerable fathers, names neither man, and is printed under the two of them together — both folders already carry the other in `related` in both directions, so it is recorded on both; «Тропарь преподобного Петра Афонского» глас 4; and «Кондак преподобного Петра» глас 2. His Russian life page life1288 was linked and NOT READ, this folder already carrying a life off three other calendars. Not checked: azbyka.ru.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 12 iunie — «Sfântul Cuvios Petru Athonitul»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 12ης Ιουνίου — «Όσιος Πέτρος ο Θεοφόρος ο εν Άθω ασκήσας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 12 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries. It is plainly the same man: the Constantinopolitan soldier taken captive and imprisoned at Samara in Mesopotamia, freed by a wonder, tonsured at Rome, who lived fifty-three years on Athos and died in a cave, his relics found by a hunter. The page contradicts itself on the date and no `dates` are recorded from it: its head line brackets him «(; - 734)» while the narrative says «έζησε κατά τον 9ο αιώνα μ.Χ.» and has him tonsured by Pope Gregory IV, who was pope from 827. The page records portions of his relics at the monasteries of Saint Dionysiou and Docheiariou on Athos and at Leimonos on Lesbos. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 25.06.2026 (12. јун ст. ст.) — „Преподобни Петар Атонски“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 12 June is the same menologion number the folder’s `romanian` and `greek` rows already carry, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed. A THIRD BOOK, A THIRD CENTURY, AND `dates` STAYS EMPTY. The folder deliberately holds no `dates`, and its `greek` note says why: saint.gr brackets him «(; - 734)» while its own narrative puts him in the ninth century and has him tonsured by a pope who was not pope until the ninth. This book states a year flat and it is neither: „Скончао 374. године“. Three books, three centuries, irreconcilable — so `dates` is **not** touched, and the Prologue’s year is stated in the life where a reader can weigh it against the note. Widening would reach from the fourth century to the ninth and would say nothing true. TWO VISITANTS IN THE PRISON, AND NEITHER IS NAMED IN THE PROSE. The wonder is that „свети Симеон Богопримац са светим Николом“ appeared to him in the gaol and touched the fetters with a staff, so that they melted like wax and he found himself outside the city. `symeon-the-god-receiver` **is** the man the epithet Богопримац names, and so the identification is not the difficulty; the second is a bare «свети Никола» with no see, no day and no epithet, and the corpus keeps many. Rather than name one visitant and leave his companion a blank in the same sentence, **both are left out of the paragraph** — `related-floor` reads a prose name as well as a linked one, and no `related` row is written in either direction. A refused identification and a deliberate omission, both recorded here. The Most Holy Богородица, who in a dream appointed him the Holy Mountain, takes no row either. WHAT ELSE IS NEW. That he was a Greek by birth and a soldier by trade; the war against the Arabs and his capture, the fetters and the gaol in the city of Samara on the Euphrates; his one prayer, to be let out into some desert; the escape; the road to Rome and the tonsure **at the tomb of the Apostle Peter by the pope himself**, whom this book does not name; the ship back east; that he had not so much as heard of the Holy Mountain before the dream; the cave and the fifty-three years in it, against hunger and thirst, heat and frost, and most of all the demons; the bread an angel brought every forty days once he had passed the first trials; the tempter appearing several times as an angel of light and driven off by the sign of the cross and the name of the Пресвета Богородица; the hunter who was hunting deer on Athos and found him a year before his death and had the life from his own mouth. And the entry’s last sentence, „Мошти му пренете у Македонију“ — his relics were translated to Macedonia. **That is a translation of relics and §5 makes it a feast and not a folder**; it is narrated in the life and takes no row and no second day. `types` UNTOUCHED: `venerable` and `hermit` are both there already; Преподобни is `venerable` and the fifty-three years in a cave are the hermit the folder already states. The soldiering is in the body as a trade and `soldier` is not added, because **a rank in the heading is written and a rank read off a sentence of the body is not** — the heading says Преподобни and nothing else. No `office`, no `locations`, no `related`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.

hymns.text: Dumnezeul părinţilor noştri, Care faci pururea cu noi după blândeţile Tale, nu îndepărta mila Ta de la noi; ci pentru rugăciunile lor, în pace îndreptează viaţa noastră.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Cuvios Petru Athonitul; the page prints the common troparion of venerable fathers, naming no saint in the text.

english.text: O God of our fathers, who dealest with us always according to Thy gentleness, take not Thy mercy from us; but at their prayers guide our life in peace.

hymns.text: Τῶν Ἀγγέλων τὸν βίον ἐν σαρκὶ μιμησάμενοι, ὤφθητε ἐρήμου πολίται, καὶ χαρίτων κειμήλια, Ὀνούφριε Αἰγύπτου καλλονή, καὶ Πέτρε τῶν ἐν Ἄθῳ ὁ φωστήρ· διὰ τοῦτο τοὺς ἀγῶνας ὑμῶν ἀεί, τιμῶμεν ἀναμέλποντες· δόξα τῷ ἐνισχύσαντι ὑμᾶς, δόξα τῷ στεφανώσαντι, δόξα τῷ ἐνεργούντι δι' ὑμῶν πάσιν ἰάματα.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος α’, Τῆς ἐρήμου πολίτης — the one apolytikion on the page of «Όσιος Πέτρος ο Θεοφόρος ο εν Άθω ασκήσας», and it names him with Onuphrius of Egypt

english.text: Having imitated in the flesh the life of the angels, you were shown to be citizens of the desert and treasuries of graces — Onuphrius, the beauty of Egypt, and Peter, the luminary of those on Athos. Therefore we honour your contests always, singing: Glory to him who gave you strength, glory to him who crowned you, glory to him who through you works healings for all.

hymns.text: Ὡς τῆς ἐρήμου πολιστὰς οὐρανοβάμονας Καὶ δωρεῶν τῶν ὑπὲρ φύσιν καταγώγια, Τὸν Ὀνούφριον ὑμνήσωμεν σὺν τῷ Πέτρῳ· Ὁ μὲν ὤφθη ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ φοῖνιξ εὔκαρπος, Ὁ δὲ ἔλαμψεν ἐν Ἄθῳ ὡς ἰσάγγελος· Τούτοις λέγοντες, θεοφόρητοι χαίρετε.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος πλ. δ’, Τῇ ὑπερμάχῳ — the one kontakion on the page of «Όσιος Πέτρος ο Θεοφόρος ο εν Άθω ασκήσας», and it names him with Onuphrius

english.text: As settlers of the desert who walked in heaven, and as lodgings of gifts beyond nature, let us hymn Onuphrius together with Peter: the one appeared in Egypt as a fruitful palm, the other shone on Athos as an equal of the angels; and let us say to them: Rejoice, you who are borne by God.

hymns.text: Φῶς νοητὸν καὶ οὐράνιον, Πέτρε λαβὼν ἐν καρδίᾳ σου, τῆς ἀκηράτου Τριάδος δοχεῖον ὤφθης λαμπρότατον, καὶ χάριν τῶν θαυμάτων ἀπείληφας, κραυγάζων, Ἀλληλούϊα.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος πλ. δ’, Πίστιν Χριστοῦ — printed on the page of «Όσιος Ονούφριος ο Αιγύπτιος», although it names Peter and not Onuphrius; it is taken here as Peter's own and is not taken on Onuphrius's folder

english.text: Having received the noetic and heavenly light in your heart, O Peter, you were shown to be a most radiant vessel of the undefiled Trinity, and you received the grace of wonders, crying: Alleluia.

hymns.text: Боже отец наших,/ творяй присно с нами по Твоей кротости,/ не отстави милость Твою от нас,/ но молитвами их// в мире управи живот наш.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 12 июня ст. ст. — «Тропарь преподобных Онуфрия и Петра»

english.text: O God of our fathers, who dealest with us ever according to thy gentleness, take not away thy mercy from us, but by their prayers guide our life in peace.

hymns.text: Мир оставил еси, Петре, Господа ради своего/ и крест восприим на рамо свое,/ на гору достигл еси Афонскую,/ якоже древле фесвитянин Илия./ И в ней пребыв пощением, и молитвами, и бдением,/ Бога милостива творя,/ и Пречистую Богородицу Молебницу предлагая,/ сего ради вопием ти:/ моли Христа Бога, да спасет души наша.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 12 июня ст. ст. — «Тропарь преподобного Петра Афонского»

english.text: Thou didst leave the world, O Peter, for thy Lord's sake, and taking thy cross upon thy shoulder thou didst reach the mountain of Athos, as the Tishbite prophet had done of old; and abiding there in fasting and prayers and vigil, making God merciful and setting forth the most pure Theotokos as thine intercessor, therefore do we cry to thee: pray to Christ God that he may save our souls.

hymns.text: Удалив себе человеческаго сожительства,/ в пещерах каменных и разселинах пожил еси,/ желанием Божественным и любовию, Петре, Господа твоего,/ от Негоже венец приял еси.// Моли непрестанно спастися нам.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 12 июня ст. ст. — «Кондак преподобного Петра»

english.text: Having withdrawn thyself from the dwelling together of men, thou didst live in caves of stone and in clefts of the rock, out of divine longing and love for thy Lord, O Peter, from whom thou hast received a crown. Pray without ceasing that we may be saved.
